h34s `NEXT_VERSION`. This placeholder collects notes for the next release while the work lands. The version is not decided yet.

## Verified since `0.2.0-alpha.1`

- **PostgreSQL 16.** The ZIO demo's Skunk Notes routes ran in a production build against PostgreSQL 16.15 with `scram-sha-256` authentication. `POST /api/notes` answered 201, invalid input answered 422, and `GET /api/notes` listed the note. Skunk's SCRAM login worked in the bundle. After `SIGTERM`, the server exited with status 0 and no session stayed open. See the [compatibility matrix](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/compatibility.md#locally-verified-in-a-cloud-session-2026-10-19).
- **kyo-sql.** The kyo-sql code in the [database guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/database.md#run-the-kyo-sql-tests) ran against PostgreSQL 16 in Node: insert and list, a unique violation mapped to a `SafeError`, two rollbacks, and a nested transaction that rolls back only its own part. A new opt-in suite, `KyoSqlPostgresSuite`, runs it when `H34S_POSTGRES_URL` is set. It has not run inside a Nitro bundle.
- **Build memory.** The cause of the demo's large build heap is now measured. Nitro bundles the linked Scala.js twice in one process: once for the prerendered Nuxt Content route and once for the server, with source maps. Without the new `scalaPrerender: 'stub'` option, the demo's `nuxt build` needs more than 4 GiB of heap (6144 MiB passed in one run). With it, a 4096 MiB heap limit passed. The scripts keep `--max-old-space-size=8192`. See the [development guide](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/development.md#production-build). <!-- claude 2026-10-19: changed: the result with scalaPrerender: 'stub' -->

## Changes

- **PostgreSQL in CI.** A new `postgres` job in the Scala.js libraries workflow runs PostgreSQL 16 with SCRAM, the kyo-sql suite, the demo's production build, `smoke.mjs` and a `SIGTERM` session check. It runs on pull requests and pushes to `main` that touch the libraries or the example; it does not run on release tags. Its first run failed on a wrong session count; the [corrected job](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/actions/runs/39277276171/job/118144813255) passed on pull request #45.
- **`scalaPrerender: 'stub'`.** The Nuxt module `@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt` has a new option. With `'stub'`, a production build keeps the linked Scala.js out of Nitro's prerender bundle, so a build that prerenders routes bundles the Scala.js once. While Nuxt prerenders, every Scala.js route answers 501; the server output does not change. If a prerendered page calls a Scala.js route anyway, h34s logs the request, and the build stops after prerendering with a list of those requests, because a page that catches the 501, as `useFetch` does, would be saved with its error state. The default, `'bundle'`, keeps the earlier behavior, and other values are a `TypeError`. The demo uses the option: its prerendering took 3.6 to 3.8 seconds instead of 47 to 59, and its build passed with a 4096 MiB heap limit. `@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt/rollup` also exports the plugin, `scalaPrerenderStub`. The packed-module check (`pnpm test:package`) builds a Nuxt application with the option. The option ships with the next `@yuri4n/h34s-nuxt` release. See [npm tooling](https://github.com/yuri4n/h34s/blob/vNEXT_VERSION/docs/npm-tooling.md#keep-scalajs-out-of-the-prerender-bundle). <!-- claude 2026-10-19: created: the scalaPrerender option (issue #30), its build error and its real-build check (review F1, F2) -->

## Alpha limits

- kyo-sql inside a Nitro bundle and other Nitro presets remain unverified.
- The demo's production build needs more than 4 GiB of Node heap without `scalaPrerender: 'stub'`. With the stub (measured with an equivalent temporary hook), it still needs more than Node's 2240 MiB default on a 15.7 GiB cloud VM. Its scripts pass 8 GiB. <!-- claude 2026-10-19: changed: the limit with the stub; the 2240 MiB run used a temporary hook (review F3) -->
